questions.q: Why can't you track field history changes on a formula field the way you can on a regular stored field?
options: Field history tracking is disabled for all custom objects
Formula fields can only exist on standard objects
Field history tracking only works on validation rules
Formula fields aren't stored — nothing is ever written or changed, it's recalculated on every view
questions.explain: Because a formula field's value is computed fresh every time it's viewed rather than saved to the database, there's no stored 'change' event to track.

questions.q: What determines which functions and nesting are legal inside a formula field?
options: The object's sharing model
The field's return type (Text, Number, Date, Checkbox, etc.)
Whether the object uses master-detail relationships
The user's profile
questions.explain: A formula field must resolve to its declared return type — mismatched types (e.g. returning text from a Number-typed formula) are a common build error.

questions.q: What does BLANKVALUE() do in a formula?
options: Substitutes a default value when the referenced field is empty
Deletes a field's value
Converts a number to text
Blocks the record from saving when a field is blank
questions.explain: BLANKVALUE() supplies a fallback when a field is null, which matters because math functions can error on a null instead of silently returning zero.

questions.q: A formula field on Contact references Account.Owner.Name. What happens if you try to use that formula to change the Account Owner's name?
options: It updates the Account Owner's name automatically
It throws a validation error
Nothing — cross-object formula references are read-only and never write back to the related record
It creates a new Account Owner record
questions.explain: Cross-object formula fields only read related data; they have no mechanism to write values back to the referenced object.

questions.q: Which scenario is a POOR fit for a formula field?
options: Concatenating First Name and Last Name into a Full Name display
Freezing a discount percentage at the exact value it had when a deal was won, even after related records later change
Displaying a calculated 'High Value' vs 'Standard' label based on Amount
Pulling an Account's Industry onto a related Contact record for use in a report filter
questions.explain: A formula field recalculates every time it's viewed, so it can never 'freeze' a value at a point in time — that requires a stored field set once by a workflow field update or Flow assignment.
